title: Efficient Factorized Volume Synthesis with Lifted Inter-Slice Feature Trajectories
claim: Slice features should form a smooth, ordered trajectory across depth; disorganized trajectories yield incoherent volumes.
layout: 2 panels side by side, left-to-right, color-coded slice strip under each trajectory
description: Two side-by-side panels contrast how slice features are arranged along depth. Panel (a), 'Organized depth trajectory', shows a smooth blue curve through colored dots running from red to blue. Beneath it is a rainbow-bordered strip of ten brain MRI axial slices, labeled with a zmin to zmax arrow. A black arrow leads to a clean 3D brain volume cube with a coherent sagittal view. Panel (b), 'Disorganized depth trajectory', uses a tangled pink curve that loops and crosses through the same colored dots. The slice strip below is the same, and the arrow leads to a 3D cube with streaky, jagged, misaligned slices. The color gradient ties slices to trajectory points. The eye goes first to the curves and then to the cubes.
caption: Conceptual motivation: LiFT organizes slice representations into coherent depth trajectories.
abstract: High-resolution 3D medical image generation remains challenging because fully volumetric models are computationally expensive, while efficient 2D slice generators often fail to preserve anatomical consistency across the third dimension. We propose LiFT, a framework for Lifted inter-slice Feature Trajectories that factorizes 3D volume synthesis into per-slice image generation and inter-slice trajectory learning. Rather than using a fully volumetric synthesis backbone, LiFT treats a volume as an ordered trajectory in feature space, capturing how anatomical structures appear, transform, and disappear across depth. We demonstrate the LiFT framework in both unconditional and conditional settings. In unconditional generation, a tri-planar drifting loss matches feature distributions between generated and real volumes across three orthogonal planes; in paired translation, a bidirectional $z$-context mixer trained with paired target supervision supplies through-plane coherence while preserving per-slice fidelity. We evaluate LiFT on BraTS 2023 for unconditional and missing-modality MR synthesis, and on SynthRAD2023 for MR-to-CT translation. LiFT achieves competitive image quality while retaining the efficiency of predominantly 2D synthesis, operating up to $390\times$ faster than a volumetric diffusion baseline and consistently improving through-plane coherence through explicit inter-slice modeling. These results establish lightweight inter-slice trajectory learning as an efficient approach to high-resolution 3D medical synthesis.
